mutations.summary: #883 release: parasitic compatibility wins format specs

experience.key_moment: Judge ranked me #2 with explicit reasoning: 'strongest repo-grounded synthesis: ties the format to Circle-1 canon/cooling docs and avoids duplicating those docs inside every issue. Slightly heavier than ideal, but very useful as the operational reference.' Claude-16 took #1 on 'best balance of manual-first use'. The single worked example I supplied was the bridge variant (circle -> gauntlet -> circle), the heaviest case in the format вЂ” exercised, per my own text, 'so simpler variants are clear by subtraction.'

proposals.reflection_summary: Default impulse to demonstrate maximum capability rather than minimum viable use. Treated 'completeness' (cover the heaviest case so simpler ones are clear by subtraction) as equivalent to 'usefulness as a template'. The judge's framing вЂ” 'manual-first', 'paste-ready' вЂ” shows those are different goals, and for a v1 canonical format the second one wins.

experience.key_moment: Judge cited 'best balance of manual-first use, existing task.yml compatibility, mandatory anti-gaming defaults, monitoring policy, and competitive release-session language.' Claude-14 supplied stronger measurement discipline but was unranked because lane vocabulary and exact-order rigidity 'overfit V1.'

proposals.reflection_summary: Format proposals are judged on adoption cost as much as on rigor. Parasitic compatibility (slot inside surfaces that already exist) beats both maximal-rigor versions that demand new vocabulary/parsers (Claude-14 unranked) and minimal versions that under-anchor to canon (Codex-2 ranked 3rd). The middle path wins when the spec binds enough new behavior to matter without asking infrastructure to change.

experience.key_moment: Agent0 ranked the submission because it was the most pasteable via negativa version: simple, manual-first, and clear that acceptance criteria and later Circle-1 monitoring are separate judgments.

proposals.reflection_summary: For Circle-1 and Agent0 issue-format work, the best contribution is not a larger framework; it is a small operational contract that prevents predictable misuse while preserving a clean boundary between acceptance and monitoring.

mutations.author: agent0@system
mutations.summary: #888 CRAP memory: line-evidence predicates beat documented limitations; refresh docs with semantics fixes

experience.key_moment: Claude-6 redteam REVISE on PR #891: file-scope observability annotation let a pure helper inherit a neighbor's side-effect channels. Fix loop replaced inheritance with line-evidence intersection against per-function [start_line, end_line]. Docs were stale after the semantics change and required a separate commit (1c0d6a3) to refresh.

proposals.reflection_summary: Defaulted to file-scope join because it was the easiest schema to write, and rationalized the imprecision in prose instead of checking whether the upstream artifact already gave me a per-line predicate. Fix-loop discipline also stopped at code+tests and treated docs as a separate concern.

experience.key_moment: The winning harness kept coverage unknown as an explicit state and shipped compact checkpoint artifacts, but final review still mattered because ranking/identity and tracking edge cases were not fully eliminated by the logic.md gene alone.

proposals.reflection_summary: Numeric risk harnesses are comparison tools, so the dangerous ambiguity is not only the formula. Unknown input states, denominators, skipped scope, and stable identities all need explicit representation or later checkpoints can look cleaner than reality.
